description: This case study is the final investigation report of the US Chemical Safety Board on the pipe rupture and fire at the Chevron Richmond refinery, California, on 6 August 2012, report number 2012-03-I-CA, dated January 2015. The executive summary describes a catastrophic rupture of a 52-inch component of the 4-sidecut line of the #4 Crude Unit, which released light gas oil at about 10,800 barrels per day into a vapour cloud that engulfed 19 employees and ignited about two minutes later, six of them suffering minor injuries, and a Level 3 Community Warning System alert with a shelter-in-place advisory for Richmond, San Pablo and North Richmond. The 132 pages cover Chevron's process safety programs, mechanical integrity, emergency response and leak response, and deficiencies in industry standards. Access: free PDF download from the CSB site; no licence is stated. Coverage is one refinery and US refining regulation. Caveats: the cause statement comes from search summaries, and only the contents and executive summary were read here. It suits emergency response and hazard exposure studies of refineries, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: A 52-inch component of the 4-sidecut piping of the #4 Crude Unit ruptured, releasing light gas oil at about 10,800 barrels per day that partly vaporised into a cloud engulfing 19 employees and ignited about two minutes later, with six minor injuries; a Level 3 community warning and shelter-in-place advisory covered Richmond, San Pablo and North Richmond. The report examines process safety programs, mechanical integrity, emergency response and industry standard deficiencies, and search summaries attribute the failure to sulfidation corrosion of a low-silicon component.
